hook: Hyderabad beats Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru on *clean-air* efforts
hook_b: Hyderabad beats Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru on *clean-air* efforts
tldr: CPCB's Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026 put Hyderabad ahead of Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and Kolkata.

beats.what: Hyderabad scored 174.2 of 200 in the CPCB's Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026 and ranked 19th among million-plus cities.
beats.why: The survey scores how civic bodies tackle road dust, construction waste, vehicle and industrial pollution, and garbage.
beats.care: Money tied to the scheme is going into electric buses and EV charging points in the city.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI: Rs 100 crore under the National Clean Air Programme is sanctioned to TGSRTC for e-buses, and Rs 30 crore to TGREDCO for EV charging.

cards.q: Does Hyderabad's air feel cleaner than other big metros to you?

qs: Which parts of the city drag the score down: dust, traffic or waste burning?
Will the e-bus money show up as fewer diesel buses on your route?

facts.t: Greater Hyderabad was also named Telangana's *first Swachh city* in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26.
In 2024 Hyderabad was *6th* in Swachh Survekshan among cities over 10 lakh people.

learn.t: Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan = CPCB's yearly ranking of how well cities act to cut air pollution.

watch: How many of the NCAP-funded electric buses and EV charging stations actually roll out.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Hyd beats five other metros in Centre's clean-air survey

fact: Hyderabad tops six big metros in the Centre's clean-air survey, scoring *174.2/200*.
twist: Among all India's 10-lakh-plus cities, though, it ranks only *19th*, up three places.
